algorithms.description: Each algorithm that the component uses, with whether FIPS 140-3 approves it.

algorithm.description: The algorithm, with its key size or curve.

name.description: What the process uses it for.

only_mode.description: Whether it works in FIPS 140-3 only mode. An approved algorithm can still fail there, when its code calls the module in a way that the mode refuses.

reason.description: Why it is not approved, or why it fails in FIPS 140-3 only mode.

certificates.description: Each certificate that the component serves, from the certificates of pki cert list.

days_left.description: The days that are left until it expires.

fips_approved.description: Whether FIPS 186-5 and SP 800-131A approve the key and the signature algorithms.

issuer.description: The issuer of the certificate. The subject again for a self-signed one.

key.description: The algorithm and size of the public key, such as ECDSA P-256.

name.description: The name of the certificate, such as api or agent-metrics.

names.description: The DNS names and the IP addresses that the certificate is for: its subject alternative names.

not_before.description: When the certificate starts to be valid.

source.description: self-signed, which osapi made, or cert_file, the operator's.

state.description: ok; not made, when the component has not started on the host; or unreadable, with the reason.

subject.description: The subject of the certificate, as a distinguished name.

fips.description: The FIPS 140-3 mode, then what is not approved, by kind, or approved.

go.description: The Go version that built the component.

listeners.description: Each TLS listener of the component, with its lowest TLS version, its suites and its groups, and whether FIPS 140-3 approves them.

approved.description: Whether the listener negotiates only approved versions, suites and groups: true in FIPS 140-3 mode, where crypto/tls restricts them.

groups.description: The key exchange groups that the listener can negotiate: the configured ones, or those of crypto/tls for the process's mode.

min_version.description: The lowest TLS version that the listener accepts.

name.description: The listener, such as api, nats or metrics.

suites.description: The cipher suites that the listener can negotiate: the configured ones, or those of crypto/tls for the process's mode.

tls.description: Whether the listener serves TLS. A listener with no TLS has no other fields.

module.description: The version of the Go Cryptographic Module in the component.

reasons.description: Each reason that the component is not in FIPS 140-3 mode with only approved algorithms, as a sentence with what closes it, or with the issue that tracks it.

summary.description: The section in one line, for a table: the FIPS 140-3 verdict, then the days left of the certificate that expires first.

200.description: The TLS section of each component.

error.description: A description of the error that occurred.

reason.description: Why the request failed, as a word that a program can branch on. The HTTP status is the class of the problem; the reason is the cause, and the error is the message for a person, which can change between releases. invalid_request: the request breaks a rule, such as a missing field (400). unauthorized: no token, or a token that is not valid (401). forbidden: the token does not have the permission (403). not_found: the host or osapi does not have what the request names (404). not_managed: the item is there, but osapi did not deploy it, so osapi does not change it (409). not_installed: the host does not have a program that the request needs (409). conflict: the state of the item blocks the request, such as a create of one that exists (409). unavailable: a part that osapi depends on is down, such as NATS (503). server_error: the controller failed; its log has the cause (500).
